## Eriksen'sfuture maylieaway fromTottenham, saysPochettino

ByJonathanVeal

Tottenham Hotspur manager Mauricio Pochettino accepts that Christian Eriksen has the right to ponder a future away from the club.

The midfielder has been one of the star players for Spurs over the past few seasons as they have challenged at the top end of the Premier League but the Dane, who joined the club in August2013,isreportedtobestalling on a new deal.

Heisoutofcontractinthesummer of 2020 but if he does not sign a new deal by the end of the current season, Spurs might be forced to listen to offers in order to get true value for the Denmarkinternational.

'I'm not a person that suffers too much in this type of situation because football is dynamic,' a relaxed Pochettino said before tonight's FA Cup third round tie at Tranmere Rovers. 'Football is about interests that as managers or head coaches we sometimes cannot manage.

Tranmere striker wouldlove to cause a cup shock tonight, he tells

J amesNorwood,theTranmereRoversstriker, has scored more goals this season than Harry Kane. But as his side welcome Tottenham Hotspur in the third round of the FACuptonight, he is in no mood to give the England captain any extra motivation.

## DerrenHoward

Norwoodhasbeeninfineformthis campaignfortheLeagueTwoside andhastwomoreleaguegoalstohis namethantheEnglandskipper.

'Tottenham have no real weaknesses and they give very little away,' said Norwood. 'It is a huge task for us but one we and our fans are looking forward to. Y ou see what they are doing to Premier League teams most weeks. With their power andskill levels, they are one of the mostcomplete teams out there. Going forward, Harry Kane and [Heung-min] Son have just been incredible.'

Heisjoint-top of the League Two scoring charts with 16 - despite failing to score for his last four matches - and the former England C international captain is keen to test himself against the eight-time FA Cupwinners.

Rovers will take inspiration from NewportCounty's fine FA Cup achievements last season. Last January, the team from south Wales forced a replay against Tottenham after a memorable 1-1 draw at RodneyParade, before losing out 2-0 in the Wembley replay.

'Newport showed the way. We will have to change what we do slightly andcreate an environment that will make it difficult for them,' he added. 'Newport made it extremely tough for them and we have to look to do the same. The pitch here will not be what they are used to. We have to look for little gains and take advantage where we can.'

<!-- image -->

Since joining Tranmere from Forest Green Rovers in 2016 the former Crystal Palace and Brighton youth striker has scored 68 times in 140 appearances - he has been the ultra-dependable goal-every-twogametypeofforward.

Norwood, 28, is out of contract this summer and his chairman MarkPalios, the former FA chief executive, has already said he doesn't want to lose his main striker in the January window. An inspired performance against Spurs would increase his stock further but, the player who made his senior debut as a lightning quick 18-year-old with pink boots for Eastbourne Town Therewillbeafullhouse at Prenton Park and hopefully we can deliver a performancetobeproudof in the Ryman League South, says he just wants to concentrate on being part of something special for Tranmere.

<!-- image -->

'There will be a full house at Prenton Park and hopefully we can deliver a performance to be proud of. It would be a great time to get back on the scoresheet but we all knowhowtoughitwill be.

'It will be a proud moment,' admitted Norwood, who still favours his trademark pink boots. 'I remembermytimewithEastbourne TownandIlearntagreat deal about adult football. To go from there and then to play Tottenham in the Cup is something special.

'I started the season well but I missed a few good chances against Buryfour games ago and I haven't scored since. I had a bit of a sulk but wewentthroughtheclips and the managersaid he is pleased with the other aspects of my play. It's been very frustrating but all you can do is work hard for the team and get in the right positions.

Norwoodhashugeadmiration for his opposite number Kane and the possibility of competing against himandahostofinternational stars is reward for a decade of toil in the lower leagues. ' As a striker you have to admire what he has achieved. He seemsto get better each season. He is always in the right place and when he gets his chance, he is lethal.'

'I have had messages of support already and a few Tottenham fans have also been in touch wanting tickets and asking me not to injure any of their players!'

Ever since his days at Eastbourne, Norwoodhasalsohadthehappy knack of doing just that. Should he get just one sniff of a chance against Spurs, he will need to be just as lethal as Kane.

'In that business there are different parties that are involved, then it is about to negotiate, to talk, and see whatthe different parties want.

The 26-year-old (right) would not be out of place in any of the top sides in Europe and would be likely to earn a lucrative deal elsewhere.
